title: Forested and cleared catchments had the same pre-1957 runoff excess in long eastern Australian records, so land clearing does not explain it (52 BoM gauges, 1889-2025)
abstract: Question: long Bureau of Meteorology flow records show that south-east Australian (SE-AU) runoff at equal rain was about 20% higher before 1957 than in 1957-1996, and lower again after 1997. Measured climate does not explain these changes. Is the early high era a land-clearing effect (rabbit plague before myxomatosis, unimproved pasture), which acts only on cleared land, and does the post-1997 deficit carry a land-cover or agency fingerprint? Approach: 52 long-record CAMELS-AUS gauges (32 SE-AU, 20 northern control), BoM daily flow, SILO rain 1889-2025. A new efficiency index without a reference period: rain response from pre-1997 year-to-year changes, then a two-way fixed-effect model. Per-gauge pre-1957 excess (X57) and 2010-2025 departure, both relative to 1957-1996, against native tree cover cleared since 1750 (NVIS). 2-degree cell bootstrap. Plan and addendum written before flow-based results. Results: forested gauges (<25% cleared, n=8) had a pre-1957 excess of +25.4% of mean flow (95% CI +15.2 to +42.8), all 8 positive; cleared gauges (>=50%, n=14) +31.0% (+11.5 to +46.1); contrast +5.6 (-20.8 to +24.5); region-demeaned Spearman rho -0.18 (-0.60 to +0.21). Both groups dropped in the late 1950s (best break 1958 cleared, 1961 forested). With daily flow capped at the 90th percentile the forested excess was larger (rho -0.56). The decision 'no land-cover fingerprint' held in all six variants. The 2010-2025 deficit also had no land-cover fingerprint (rho -0.14). All agencies had an excess (VIC +18, NSW +40, QLD +18). As a replication, the SE-AU 1997-2025 mean was 13.3 points (-19.9 to -8.0) below the 1924-1996 mean, outside AR(1), AR(2) and sample-autocovariance nulls (P 0.006-0.011; <=0.023 in all variants). The early excess was mostly in high flows; the post-1997 deficit remains in ordinary flows. No low-frequency driver fitted before 1997 predicted the deficit; 20-year rain memory predicted a surplus. Conclusion: the pre-1957 high era is not a land-clearing effect; a cause that acts on forested and cleared catchments alike (an unmeasured climate factor or flow measurement, such as extrapolated early high-flow ratings) is needed. The post-1997 deficit is a separate event in ordinary flows, not one multidecadal efficiency mode. Limitations: 27 gauges with early data in 13 cells; wide contrast intervals; land cover from about 2000; agency and region confounded; ratings not tested; break analysis post hoc; tests T1-T4 replicate sibling bundles.

citations.reason: We use its 58 long-record gauges and its BoM flow and SILO recipes (our rebuilt tables are byte-identical) and test the cause of the pre-1957 high efficiency that it found.
We replicate its stationary-null and climate-driver results with a reference-free index; its open question (catchment change or measurement) is the subject of our land-cover test.
Its climate-adjusted efficiency fell near 1957; we find the same late-1950s drop in both cleared and forested catchments.
It found that the 1937-1960 high era was a flood-flow excess; our capped-flow index agrees and shows the post-1997 deficit in ordinary flows.
Our SE-AU minus North contrast after 2010 is also inside its earlier range.
It separated the earlier lows from the post-1997 slope loss; we separate the early excess from the late deficit by flow range and test land cover.
It suggested land development as a candidate for the pre-1957 surplus; our forested catchments had the same surplus.
It found no protected-area effect on the post-1997 deficit; our clearing gradient also shows none.
Its post-1997 rain-response loss is the deficit we place against a century of variation.
Its persistent low-runoff state is the post-1997 state that our stationary null tests.
It found different timing in Victoria and NSW; we compare state agencies for the early excess.
Fire effects are a limitation of our forested-group test.
It excluded greening as a post-1997 cause; we test land cover for the earlier excess.
